text.en: Create a Test Readiness Checklist for every major test.
Are temporary components removed or identified?
Is insulation complete where required before test?
Are open deficiencies affecting the test resolved?
Have previous test failures been closed?
Is electrical power available where required?
Is the system safe to energize/pressurize/start?
Do not approve readiness from paperwork alone.
drawing → physical system → equipment tag → connections → access → test boundary
The system should be complete enough that the test evaluates performance, not unfinished construction.
NOT READY → READY WITH HOLD ITEMS → READY FOR TEST → TESTED
AHU start-up scheduled, but condensate drain is incomplete and controls are not connected.
Do not conduct meaningless start-up just because contractor is mobilized.
Record readiness failure → identify missing prerequisites → assign → complete → re-walk system → release start-up only when appropriate.
Recheck every previously open readiness item.
This helps identify why commissioning is slipping.

qualityObjective.en:
Confirm that a system is genuinely ready to be tested before testing begins, so results are meaningful and test failures are not caused by incomplete construction or poor preparation.
This is one of the most important commissioning controls because premature testing wastes time and can produce misleading results.

authorityNote.en: The project drawings, devis, Plan Qualite, PIE/PRIE, approved procedures, professional instructions and CRT/Hydro-Quebec requirements govern. This playbook tells you how to systematically find, verify, document and close the quality requirements; it does not replace them.

text.en: Before test, prepare the record so nobody is trying to reconstruct details afterward.
Documentation should capture the actual instruments used.
Pressure gauge PG-12 → Calibration certificate CAL-021 → valid through date X
do not backfill data from memory later;
Never erase the history of a failure.
initial failure → corrective action → retest → acceptance
Complete missing information only with valid traceable evidence.
If a required test cannot be substantiated
determine whether the test must be repeated.
Track missing/incomplete test records because paperwork backlog can become a turnover risk even when physical construction is complete.

qualityObjective.en:
Ensure every test is supported by complete, legible, traceable and technically attributable documentation showing what was tested, how, by whom, with what equipment, against what criterion, and with what result.
A test without traceable documentation is weak evidence.

text.en: piping installed → pressure test → repair/retest → flush → insulate → start equipment → control verification → balancing → functional test
Specialized performance acceptance remains with authorized mechanical/commissioning personnel.
Identify test zone → locate leakage points → repair seams/joints → repeat complete required test → document both initial fail and final pass.

qualityObjective.en:
This consolidates the testing interfaces from our Mechanical module.
Demonstrate that installed mechanical systems are leak-free, clean, operational and capable of meeting specified functional requirements through controlled testing and specialist acceptance.

text.en: Check evidence for calibrated specialist test instruments.
Is the correct equipment being tested?
Is the approved test being used?
Did a failed test trigger corrective action and retest?
Exact technical criteria come from authorized electrical procedures/personnel.
Failure → control status → electrical specialist diagnoses → corrective work → retest → specialist acceptance.
Verify process completion, not technical reinterpretation.

qualityObjective.en:
We keep the technical-authority boundary firm.
Ensure required electrical tests are planned, traceable and documented, with technical acceptance provided by authorized electrical specialists and all failures fully closed before energization/turnover.

text.en: Window water test fails at sill corner.
Do not simply add sealant indiscriminately.
Identify actual water path → inspect sill/jamb/flashing interface → apply approved corrective method → repeat same test → document passing retest.
Retest the corrected assembly using required method.
repeated failures at same interface type.

qualityObjective.en: Demonstrate that the completed building envelope achieves required water, air and membrane-integrity performance at the tested assemblies and interfaces.

text.en: Input → expected response → actual response → acceptance
BAS calls for fan ON → fan starts → status feedback confirms → airflow condition achieved.
Your role may be to witness/document rather than technically commission.
Ensure relevant equipment/devices are installed and ready.
Complex logic should be accepted by controls/fire/electrical/mechanical commissioning specialists.
alarm input doesn't trigger expected interface.
Identify responsible system/trade → correct → repeat full affected function.
Verify end-to-end function, not just replaced component.

text.en: Again, technical acceptance belongs to appropriate specialist.
Pump starts but exhibits abnormal vibration.
Do not simply leave it running.
Stop/control per responsible specialist → document → inspect alignment/support/installation → specialist diagnosis → correction → repeat start-up → retain passing record.
Track startup failures, shipping damage, installation-related startup issues.

qualityObjective.en: Ensure equipment is initially started under controlled conditions, in accordance with manufacturer/project procedures, with installation prerequisites complete and start-up data properly recorded.

text.en: every individual system must be substantially tested first;
Do not use integrated testing to discover that basic individual systems were never completed.
Does system return to correct state?
Ensure relevant systems and test tools available.
Fire alarm signal correctly activates but associated damper does not close.

Record interface failure → determine whether mechanical actuator, fire-alarm signal, controls, or wiring is responsible → correct responsible component/system → repeat full scenario → verify all related responses → close.
Retest the integrated sequence, not merely the failed component.
Track interface failures separately because they expose coordination weaknesses.

text.en: Never replace original failed test with later passing test.
If failure involves defective component/material, control the affected item.
A failed test may itself trigger
depending on CRT procedure and significance.
Actual corrective action depends on specialist diagnosis.
Your control responsibility is making sure it is authorized, performed, verified and retested.
This becomes a useful management dashboard

qualityObjective.en:
This deserves its own workflow because failures must never disappear inside paperwork.
Ensure every failed test is immediately identifiable, controlled, investigated, corrected, retested and traceably closed without losing the original failure record.

text.en: Do not weaken acceptance criteria simply because this is a retest.
do not cycle repairs indefinitely without analysis.
Retest report → original failure → corrective action
Confirm passing retest and specialist acceptance.
Repeated retests are a strong signal for root-cause/trend review.

qualityObjective.en: Confirm that corrective work actually resolves the failed condition by repeating the required test under valid conditions and maintaining traceability to the original failure.

text.en: That package tells the whole story.
Confirm final installed equipment/material identification matches acceptance records.
System physically works, but required manufacturer start-up sheet is missing.
Track missing acceptance evidence → obtain valid manufacturer/startup documentation or repeat required activity if necessary → complete acceptance package.
Physical completion and documentary completion are both required.
Requirement → inspection → test → failure history → corrective action → retest → acceptance → turnover evidence
Can the entire chain be reconstructed?

qualityObjective.en:
This is the final output of the entire testing/commissioning system.
Compile a complete, traceable body of evidence demonstrating that each system has been inspected, tested, corrected where necessary, accepted by the appropriate authority and is ready for turnover.
